newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WELSH RESOLVE POWER STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WELSH RESOLVE POWER STRUGGLE.

text.p: Welsh rugby union officials reached a truce with their first division clubs on Monday, ending a year-long power struggle over television rights and money.
The agreement sets a precedent for the Rugby Football Union which resumes talks with England's professional clubs on Tuesday in an attempt to thrash out a similar peace formula.
The Welsh have agreed to form an eight-member joint management committee to run the professional game. The clubs and the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) will be represented by four members each.
In addition, the WRU agreed to fund the clubs for the current season.

"I firmly believe that today's meeting and the concensus it has achieved is the biggest thing that has happened to Welsh rugby since the 1999 Rugby World Cup was awarded to Wales," said WRU chairman Vernon Pugh.
